To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
medicalization is a process that occurs in the social world of medical care and in the social world outside of that of medical care.
medicalization occurs at three levels: conceptual, institutional, and interpersonal.

(1) medicalization is a process that occurs on multiple levels of analysis, including the doctor-patient interaction, conceptual, and institutional levels; (2) medicalization is not a process of “imperialism”; (3) medicalization is the result of a complex set of factors that are not reducible to one cause; and (4) medicalization is an ongoing process and not an event.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the medicalization thesis as a conceptual framework and not as a theory of medical imperialism.

medicalization occurs at multiple levels and that the concept of medicalization is a powerful tool for understanding the social and historical development of medicine.
